# muxt test runs the tests on muxt's template engine, and that engine does
# not escape every attribute the way html/template does. The test below
# asserts html/template's output for a Datastar attribute, which html/template
# treats as JavaScript: it passes under go test and fails under muxt test.
# The failure is the finding: run go test, read the differences. The script
# asserts that the test fails, not what the engine writes, since the
# engine's escaping is expected to change.

exec go test ./...
stdout '^ok  \tserver\t'

! muxt test
stdout 'FAIL'
stdout 'data-on-click'
! stderr .

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- index.gohtml --
<button data-on-click="{{.Action}}">Load</button>
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Action string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "index.gohtml", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestDatastarAttribute(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Action: "@get('/x?a=1&b=2')"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// html/template writes the ampersand as a JavaScript escape, a backslash
	// and u0026, inside the HTML-escaped quotes.
	want := `<button data-on-click="&#34;@get(&#39;/x?a=1` + `\` + `u0026b=2&#39;)&#34;">Load</button>` + "\n"
	if got := buf.String(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("data-on-click page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
